message.content:
Add "bring your own Deepgram key" (BYOK) to the Earshot **Chrome extension** in /Users/rizelscarlett/Documents/agent-experiments/voice-experiments/live-captions/apps/extension (WXT 0.21, MV3, React, Tailwind v4). Another agent is changing `apps/web` at the same time — don't touch it, and don't edit `packages/shared` (report shared bugs instead). Don't run `npm install`, don't commit, don't touch any process on port 3000 (unrelated project). Never print API key values.

Read first: `apps/extension/README.md`, `utils/messages.ts`, `utils/config.ts`, `entrypoints/background.ts`, `entrypoints/offscreen/main.ts`, `entrypoints/sidepanel/App.tsx`, `entrypoints/popup/App.tsx`; and in packages/shared: `src/core/session.ts`, `src/core/deepgram.ts`, `src/core/types.ts`, `src/core/token.ts`.

## Goal
The owner wants people to use the extension without the owner paying for their Deepgram usage, and ideally without needing any Earshot server at all.
- **User key mode (new):** the user pastes their own Deepgram API key in the extension. It's stored in `chrome.storage.local` only, and the offscreen document opens the Deepgram WebSocket directly with it. No Earshot server needed — the extension works standalone.
- **Server mode (keep working):** with no user key, the extension uses the Earshot server's token endpoint as today (`POST {serverUrl}/api/deepgram/token`, default http://localhost:3100). The owner uses this locally; don't regress it.
- A saved user key takes precedence over the server.

## Already in packages/shared
- `TranscriptionSession({ getToken })` — `getToken` may return a `string` (bearer JWT) or `DeepgramCredential` `{ type: "token", value: userKey }`. With a user key, a handshake failure on the first connect ends the session with status `error` and a message containing "API key" (no retry loop).
- `verifyDeepgramKey(key) → Promise<"ok" | "rejected" | "offline">` (briefly opens a socket; Deepgram's REST API has no browser CORS) and `looksLikeDeepgramKey(key)`.
- The web server will expose `GET {serverUrl}/api/deepgram/token` → `{ serverKey: boolean }` (being added now by the web agent); POST without a server key returns 503 `{ error, code: "no_server_key" }`.

## What to build
- Offscreen documents only get `chrome.runtime`, so pass the credential choice in the start message from the background: background reads the user key from storage and sends `{ userKey }` or the server URL; offscreen builds `getToken` accordingly (user key → `{type:"token", value}`; otherwise `createTokenFetcher`). Keep the key out of logs and out of messages broadcast to pages and content scripts — only background → offscreen.
- Side panel settings: a "Deepgram key" section above Server URL: password input with show/hide, "Verify & save" (uses `verifyDeepgramKey` from the side panel page), inline errors, "Forget key", status line "Using your key (••••last4)" or "Using Earshot server at …". Link to https://console.deepgram.com/ with a note to create a dedicated key with minimal permissions and an expiry. Privacy line: the key stays in this browser and only goes to Deepgram.
- First run: if there's no user key and the server isn't reachable or reports `serverKey:false`, the popup and side panel should explain that a key is needed and link straight to the key setting (popup → open side panel settings view), instead of failing later with a network error. When an active session fails with an "API key" error, show a "Check your key" action.
- Manifest: no new permissions; WebSocket to Deepgram from the offscreen document needs no host permission (verify that in practice).
- Update `apps/extension/README.md`: standalone use with your own key (no server), server mode, privacy notes.

## Verify (report real outputs)
- `npx wxt build` and `npx tsc --noEmit -p apps/extension` pass; manifest permissions unchanged.
- Real flow with your own key and **no Earshot server running on 3100**: adapt the existing headful smoke test at /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-rizelscarlett-Documents-agent-experiments-voice-experiments-live-captions/81ecccbe-aa1d-4f97-8070-a49b0e80faab/scratchpad/smoke.mjs (run with `headful` — headless captures silent audio). Copy it to a new file, set the key via the side panel UI (read the key from apps/web/.env.local into an env var without printing it), start captions on the local test media page and assert real transcript lines arrive in the side panel and overlay. Also assert a bad key shows the rejected message, and that "Forget key" clears it. Skip the service-worker-kill step (it wedges Chrome).
- Server mode regression: if the web agent has a server running on 3100 when you get there, run the original smoke flow without a user key; otherwise start `npm run start -w @earshot/web` only if a build exists in apps/web/.next and port 3100 is free, and stop it afterwards. If you can't, say so.
- Stop every server/browser you started; delete temp browser profiles.

Final report: files changed, behaviour in both modes, verification outputs, anything not verified.

### Standalone: bring your own key (no server)

1. Create a key at [console.deepgram.com](https://console.deepgram.com/). Make a **dedicated key for Earshot** with the fewest permissions (Member or lower) and an **expiry date**, so you can revoke it without touching anything else.
2. Open the side panel → **Settings** → **Deepgram key**, paste it and press **Verify & save**. Earshot briefly opens a Deepgram streaming socket to check the key (Deepgram's REST API doesn't allow browser requests). Rejected, malformed or unverifiable (offline) keys are not saved.
3. The status line reads "Using your key (••••last4)". **Forget key** removes it.

That's it: no Earshot server, no build-time config. Usage is billed to your Deepgram account. If Deepgram rejects a saved key when you start (deleted or expired), captions stop with an error and a **Check your key** button instead of retrying.

How it flows: the background service worker reads the key from `chrome.storage.local` when you press Start and passes it to the offscreen document in the `start` message (`credential: { kind: "user-key" }`). The offscreen document opens `wss://api.deepgram.com/v1/listen` with Deepgram's `token` subprotocol. No host permission is needed for that WebSocket.

**Privacy**
- The key is stored only in this browser profile (`chrome.storage.local`), is never synced, and is only ever sent to Deepgram. It never goes to an Earshot server or anywhere else.
- It is never logged, never shown in full after saving (only the last 4 characters), and never sent to web pages or the caption overlay. Content scripts never receive it in a message. The only message that carries it is the background → offscreen `start` command.
- Like anything in extension storage, it is readable by someone with access to your Chrome profile on disk. That's why a dedicated, limited, expiring key is recommended.

### Server mode (Earshot token endpoint)

With no key saved, each connect asks the Earshot web app for a short-lived token, and the permanent key stays on the server:

- `POST {EARSHOT_URL}/api/deepgram/token` with body `{}` returns `{ access_token, expires_in }` (503 `{ code: "no_server_key" }` when the server has no key).
- `GET {EARSHOT_URL}/api/deepgram/token` returns `{ serverKey: boolean }`. The popup, side panel and Start use it to tell up front whether the server can help. - The server allows CORS from `chrome-extension://` origins.

- **Default:** `http://localhost:3100`. Run the web app with `npm run dev:web` from the repo root, with `DEEPGRAM_API_KEY` in `apps/web/.env.local`.
- **At build time:** `WXT_EARSHOT_URL=https://earshot.example.com npx wxt build`.
- **At runtime:** side panel → **Settings** → **Server URL**. The value is saved in `chrome.storage.local` and used the next time you press Start. **Reset** returns to the build-time default. It's ignored while your own key is saved.

open(p,'w').write(s)
EOF

content.text:
BYOK is in the extension and works without any Earshot server: with my own key and nothing listening at the server URL, real captions reached both the side panel and the in-page overlay. Server mode still works. `npx wxt build` and `npx tsc --noEmit -p apps/extension` both pass, and the manifest permissions are unchanged (`tabCapture, offscreen, sidePanel, storage, activeTab, scripting`, no host permissions).

**How it behaves**
- **Your own key:** the key is stored in `chrome.storage.local` under `deepgramKey`. When you press Start, the background reads it and passes it to the offscreen document in the start message; that is the only message that carries it. The offscreen document then connects to Deepgram directly. A saved key always wins, and the Earshot server is never contacted.
- **Server mode:** with no key saved, the background first checks the server with `GET /api/deepgram/token`, then uses the existing token fetcher. If the server is unreachable or reports `serverKey:false`, Start fails straight away with a "needs a Deepgram API key" message and an "Add your Deepgram key" button, without starting capture.
- **Side panel:** the tab is now called "Settings". A "Deepgram key" section sits above Server URL with everything you specified: password field with Show/Hide, "Verify & save", inline errors, "Forget key", the status line, the console link with the dedicated-key advice, and the privacy line. When no key is available, a "needs a key" notice appears at the top.
- **Popup:** shows the same "needs a key" notice. "Add your key" opens the side panel on the key field. "Open Earshot web" is hidden when there's no server or you're using your own key.
- **"API key" errors:** if a session fails with one, both popup and side panel show "Check your key".

**Verification (both runs headful)**
- **Own key** (`smoke-byok.mjs`): all 24 checks passed, including:
  - The popup and side panel both said a key was needed.
  - "Add your key" opened the real side panel with the key field focused.
  - A bad key showed "Deepgram rejected this key" and wasn't saved; a non-key string was caught before any network call.
  - The real key saved and showed as masked; the full key never appeared in the page or any console output.
  - Real tabCapture started, 3 transcript lines arrived, the overlay showed captions and the badge said LIVE.
  - A rejected saved key ended the session with Deepgram's "didn't accept your API key" error and a "Check your key" button.
  - "Forget key" cleared storage and the status went back to "no Earshot server is reachable".
- **Server mode** (`smoke-server.mjs`, the original flow without the service-worker-kill step): passed with exit 0 and no console errors. Real capture, 3 lines, overlay hide/show, fullscreen, navigation and stop all behaved as before; no "needs a key" notice and the web link was shown.

**Things to know**
- The web agent started its own server on 3100 partway through my first run. So for the own-key test I pointed the extension at `http://localhost:3199`, where nothing is listening, to stand in for "no server". The server-mode run used the web agent's server, so I didn't start or stop any server myself.
- Not separately checked: the offscreen network capture attached after the WebSocket had opened, so "no traffic to the server" rests on the code path plus the dead server URL. The no-host-permission claim does have practical evidence: Deepgram connected from the offscreen document with no host permissions.
- The key travels in a runtime message, which extension pages (popup, side panel) also receive and ignore. Content scripts never get it. Extension pages can read the same storage anyway, so this exposes nothing new.
